entries.value: Castello Banfi ‘Florus’ Moscadello di Montalcino 2011 is late harvest Moscato Bianco from the hills of Montalcino, in Tuscany. The grapes hang on the vine to concentrate; the wine is made sweet and partly aged in oak. Fifteen years on it is golden amber: honey, apricot, orange blossom, candied orange and a little nut, with fresh acidity. It is the value bottle for the Blackberry Trifle and the Pineapple Tarte Tatin, sweeter than the lemon curd and easy with the charred fruit. We pour it at 46 to 50°F in a small dessert glass, from an ice bucket with water. Moscadello was Montalcino’s wine for centuries before Brunello.

entries.value: Domaine Huet ‘Le Mont’ Vouvray Moelleux 2009 is Chenin Blanc from Le Mont, one of Huet’s three biodynamic vineyards in Vouvray, in the Loire. Huet makes its Chenin sec, demi-sec and moelleux, and moelleux means sweet. At seventeen years, golden: honeyed quince, baked apple, chamomile and beeswax, with Chenin’s fresh acidity and a long, mineral finish. It is the classic with the Baked Apple, as sweet as its brown sugar glaze, its acidity lifting the crème fraîche. We pour it at 46 to 50°F in a small dessert glass, from an ice bucket. Victor Huet founded the domaine in 1928, and Le Mont joined it in 1957.

entries.target: wine:Château Climens Barsac Premier Cru Classé 2010
entries.value: Château Climens Barsac Premier Cru Classé 2010 is Sémillon alone, from a plateau of red sand over limestone in Barsac, one of the five communes of Sauternes. Grapes shrivelled by noble rot are picked by hand in several passes, and the wine is aged in oak. At sixteen years: candied lemon, apricot, honey and saffron, rich, with the freshness Barsac is known for. It is the classic with the Lemon Tart, its citrus meeting the yuzu and meringue. We pour it at 48 to 52°F in a small white wine glass, from an ice bucket. Ranked a first growth in 1855, it is called the Lord of Barsac.

entries.target: wine:Inniskillin Cabernet Franc Icewine Niagara Peninsula 2015
entries.value: Inniskillin Cabernet Franc Icewine Niagara Peninsula 2015 is a red icewine from Ontario, Canada, where the lakes temper the climate. The grapes freeze naturally on the vine, at minus eight degrees Celsius or colder, and are pressed frozen, leaving the water as ice and only a few drops of very sweet juice. Pale ruby: strawberry, raspberry, rhubarb and red cherry, intensely sweet, with vivid acidity. It is the classic with the Blackberry Trifle, an echo of its blackberry curd. We pour it at 46 to 50°F in a small dessert glass, from an ice bucket. Inniskillin’s Vidal Icewine 1989 won the Grand Prix d’Honneur at Vinexpo in 1991.
